name: jenson-roman-typeface
description: A Venetian printer cut an elegant roman letter whose proportions inspired revivals for centuries.

name: caxton-westminster-press
description: A merchant who had learned printing abroad set up a press at Westminster and began issuing books in English.

name: garamond-roman-type
description: A Parisian punchcutter's refined roman letters were used in a scholarly edition and became a model for generations.

name: bay-psalm-book
description: A press in a New England colony produced a hymn book, the first book printed in English-speaking North America.

name: caslon-type-specimen
description: An English engraver displayed his oldstyle typefaces, which came to dominate printing across Britain and its colonies.

name: baskerville-virgil
description: A Birmingham printer published a book showing off his sharp, high-contrast typeface and glossy paper.

name: first-sans-serif-typeface
description: A London type foundry issued a bold, plain capital letter with no serifs, which startled contemporaries.

name: sholes-typewriter-patent
description: A Milwaukee newspaperman won a patent for a practical keyboard writing machine that became the model for later typewriters.

name: remington-typewriter-sales
description: A firearms maker put the first commercial typewriter on sale, with the keyboard layout still used today.

name: johnston-london-typeface
description: A calligrapher drew a clear, humanist sans-serif alphabet for a city's railway signs and posters.

name: futura-typeface-released
description: A German designer issued a geometric typeface built from circles, triangles and squares, a modernist favourite.

name: times-new-roman-debut
description: A London newspaper commissioned a tightly spaced new typeface that later became a word-processing default.

name: helvetica-released
description: A Swiss foundry issued a neutral sans-serif typeface that spread across corporate logos and street signs worldwide.

name: ibm-selectric-typewriter
description: An electric typewriter swapped moving typebars for a spinning ball, letting users change fonts in seconds.

name: project-gutenberg-begins
description: A student typed out a famous declaration onto a university computer, starting the free electronic book library.

name: desktop-publishing-arrives
description: A laser printer, PostScript and page layout software let ordinary offices produce typeset-quality pages from a desk.

name: comic-sans-created
description: A software designer drew a casual, comic-book style typeface that became both popular and widely mocked.

name: emoji-added-to-unicode
description: The universal text standard adopted hundreds of Japanese-origin pictograms, making them part of everyday writing worldwide.
